name: Mburku
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only survey/subclassification material (Decker et al. 2022) surfaced; no phonological description with stress reached

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. Chadic and West Chadic opening pages, rogerblench.info (Internet Archive copy 2025-05-27/28).
sources.note: Index pages only; list Miya and Sirzakwai (Warji) dictionaries and A3/B3 sub-pages, no Mburku wordlist or sketch.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page mbur1239 (Hammarström et al.).
sources.note: No descriptive references at all (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); only overview/wordlist items; subclassification source Decker et al. 2022.
Consonant table compiled from Decker et al. 2022; nothing on tone, stress or vowels; only references are Ethnologue and Decker et al. 2022.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Fittokka Gobak, Yakubu Danladi, Julius Dabet, Christina Riepe, Adedamola Aregbesola, Benard Abraham, Andrew Lewinan & Thelma Araokanmi. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the West Chadic North Bauchi Languages of Bauchi and Jigawa States, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-010. SIL International. 108 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Section 6.3 'Phonetic inventory' (pp. 23-24) covers consonants/vowels only; Appendix G (p. 65) gives a tone-marked 348-item Burku wordlist (e.g. kìkʷù 'animal', hərwìː 'cow') with the caveat 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Section 3 (p. 3) lists all prior literature on Burku: Temple 1922, N. Skinner 1977, Jungraithmayr & Ibriszimow 1994, Haruna 2005 — no phonological description.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2012. Linguistic and cultural background to the North Bauchi region and the Wiihə people (finalised draft). Cambridge: ms.
sources.note: Ethnographic/historical background; Mburku appears only in the language table (Table 1: Mburku = Və Mvəran, [bbt], 12,000 speakers) and in a few comparative lexical tables (e.g. 'horse' daaku, 'hoe' tiyi) sourced to Skinner 1977 and Skinner's unpublished notes. Nothing on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Skinner, Neil. 1977. North Bauchi Chadic languages: common roots. Afroasiatic Linguistics 4(1): 1-49. Malibu: Undena.
sources.note: Comparative wordlist of nine North Bauchi languages incl. Mburku ('Və Mvəran', Hausa Mburkanci, abbreviation B, informant Muhammadu Baro, p. 2). Section 2 'The phonetic inventory' (p. 5) covers the group as a whole: 'As for tones, usually three levels and a falling were heard in the recordings and a number of minimal pairs of monosyllables confirmed, but it would have been highly impressionistic to have included any tonal markings in the present work.' No mention of stress or accent; no Mburku-specific prosodic statement.

sources.citation: Haruna, Andrew. 2005. The endangered languages issue in Northern Nigeria: a Chadic perspective. Borno Museum Society Newsletter 62/63: 7-32.

sources.note: Listed by Glottolog and Decker 2022 as a Burku source; endangerment survey, unlikely to describe stress.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1998. A Grammar of Miya. University of California Publications in Linguistics 130. Berkeley: University of California Press.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number Philol 346.20 vol. 130) (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number Philol 346.20 vol. 130
sources.note: Not a Mburku source, but the only full grammar of a North Bauchi (Warji-group) language; its tone chapter is the nearest description of the prosodic type Mburku is expected to share. Useful for an identity/family note only, not for the catalog entry.
